question: are sigma70 -35/-10 box pairs more frequent in real upstream intergenic regions than in a null built from the same regions?
what_is_not_claimed: no promoter is located and none is predicted. The boxes are information-poor and occur often by chance, so a per-operon statement would not be publishable; only the enrichment is

nulls.mononucleotide_shuffle: bases of the same region shuffled: length and base composition, so GC, are exactly preserved; dinucleotide composition is not
nulls.markov1_resample: transition probabilities learned from the same region, a new sequence of the same length generated: dinucleotide composition preserved in expectation, which closes the first null's gap
nulls.why_two: one null is an assumption. The claim is published only if both point the same way; if they diverge, the divergence is the finding

method.statistic: observed number of units carrying at least one pair against the number expected under the null (the sum of the null probabilities), tested with a two-sided binomial. A sign test on per-unit differences was tried first and was wrong: the real value is binary while the null value is a mean over replicates, so a region with no pair counted against the real data whenever the null found one in a single replicate
method.levels: entry, sequence and genus. Regions from one genome are not independent, so an entry-level p value is small by repeated sampling alone; the genus level decides
method.strand: regions were written on the strand that drives the operon by upstream_regions.py; nothing is re-complemented here

denominator.note: only replicons whose nucleotide sequence is readable could contribute; see replicon_sequence.csv and ROADMAP 135.21. Whether the result generalises to the unreadable majority is unmeasured
